definition: Self-healing test automation is a technique in software testing in which automated test scripts automatically detect, diagnose, and repair failures caused by changes in the application under test — without requiring manual intervention from a software engineer or QA professional.
details: The approach relies on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods to identify new or changed user interface elements at runtime and update broken locators accordingly, maintaining test suite stability in the face of continuous software changes.

explainer.lead: Self-healing test automation automatically detects, diagnoses, and repairs test failures caused by changes in the application under test, without manual intervention. It matters because it keeps test suites stable as software changes continuously.

tiers.eli5: When the app's buttons or fields move, the test fixes its own directions instead of a person rewriting them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on AI and ML methods to identify new or changed UI elements at runtime and update broken locators. A pitfall is that silent repairs can mask genuine application defects rather than broken tests.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, automated test scripts detect, diagnose, and repair failures caused by changes in the application under test without human intervention. It relies on AI/ML to find changed UI elements at runtime and update broken locators.

explainer.example: A login button is renamed in the app; the test fails, the system identifies the new element at runtime, and the locator is updated automatically.
